newsitem.title: USA: Clinton warns adults to keep guns from minors.
newsitem.headline: Clinton warns adults to keep guns from minors.

text.p: Trying to restrict youth gangs' access to guns, President Bill Clinton on Wednesday ordered gun stores to post signs warning adults they would be committing a felony if they sold or gave a handgun to a minor.

"I want every adult who buys a gun to see that sign and think about it before they give a child a gun that could wind up in gang violence," Clinton said in a speech to a juvenile justice conference at Georgetown University.

Clinton said he directed Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin to require all federally licensed gun dealers to "post signs in their stores and issue written warnings with each gun they sell to put adult gun purchasers on clear and unambiguous notice that selling or giving a handgun to a minor is dangerous."
He said an adult transfer of a handgun to a minor represented a felony crime that could carry a penalty of up to 10 years in prison.
Clinton said he was issuing the order in another attempt to crack down on youth violence. It requires 112,000 federally licensed firearms dealers to post the signs.
The White House issued a statement from the Fraternal Order of Police, the national police union, in support of Clinton's directive.

"The illegal guns that youth gangs use do not just come out of thin air," Clinton said. "They are bought and sold, traded and given in trade, just like any other guns. And all too often, it is adults who are making the transfer."
Clinton also used the speech to promote legislation he submitted in February that contains his prescription for battling youth violence.

His legislation would require child-safety locks be sold with guns to try to prevent accidental shootings. It would help keep schools open after hours, on weekends and in the summer to give children a place to go instead of hitting the streets.

It would also "declare war" on gangs by providing new prosecutors and tougher penalties. It would extend the Brady Bill handgun control law to bar someone who commits a crime as a juvenile from buying a gun as an adult.
A rival bill passed in May by the House of Representatives would allow juveniles as young as 13 to be tried as adults for violent crimes and drug offenses.
Clinton attacked that legislation as inadequate for the cause.

But the Republican Leadership Conference, a political organization, urged Clinton to sign the House bill in order to "once and for all get these super-predators off our streets and into the justice system where they belong."
